Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

    feat(monitor): macOS telemetry backend (CPU/RAM/GPU sparklines, no sudo)
    
    `:status` showed `CPU: n/a`, `RAM: n/a`, `GPU: none` on Apple Silicon
    because mlpl-monitor only had a Linux source (`/proc` + `nvidia-smi`); the
    facade returned `Snapshot::default()` everywhere else. Adds the macOS
    sibling so the MLX server's `/v1/stats` (and the REPL sparklines it feeds)
    report real numbers -- all without sudo:
    
    - CPU: scrape `top -l 2` (the second sample is the live interval). The
      Mach `host_statistics64` tick counters would be the library analog of
      /proc/stat, but libc's bindings are deprecated and `mach2` dropped the
      host-statistics API, so `top` is the dependency-free path.
    - RAM: `vm_stat` (active+wired+compressed pages) + `sysctl hw.memsize`.
    - GPU: `ioreg -c IOAccelerator` -> `Device Utilization %` and `In use
      system memory`; unified memory means VRAM-total is reported as total
      RAM. The macOS analog of `nvidia-smi`.
    
    The facade now selects the platform source crate via a compile-time alias,
    so `snapshot()` is written once for Linux + macOS; only `cpu_percent`
    splits (Linux windows two tick samples, macOS uses top's own interval).
    Each source keeps a pure `parse_*` (unit-tested on fixtures) behind the
    thin IO. No caller or wire change -- mlpl-serve picks it up via the
    existing mlpl-monitor dependency.
    
    Verified live on an M3 Pro: cpu ~8-11%, ram 10/18 GB, gpu "Apple M3 Pro"
    with util + 587 MB in use; `/v1/stats` returns all four.

# Saga: Stable Diffusion (text-to-image)

Active-saga plan. Full scoping + rationale lives in
`docs/future-saga-stable-diffusion.md`; this is the executable step
breakdown. Diffusion is the non-autoregressive generation path (see the
glossary [[Autoregression]] entry): start from noise, iteratively
denoise.

Strategy: ship the diffusion *algorithm* in the browser first (tiny,
no conv), then add `conv2d` for image U-Nets (GPU), then real Stable
Diffusion via candle-transformers on a connected GPU peer.

## Steps

1. **diffusion-2d-demo** -- the diffusion algorithm, browser-runnable,
   no conv. Add the two small pure-array builtins the noise schedule
   needs: `linspace(start, stop, n)` and `cumprod(v)` (TDD: unit tests +
   gradcheck where applicable). Glossary: Diffusion model, Forward
   (noising) / Reverse (denoising) process, DDPM, Noise schedule. A
   `demos/diffusion_2d.mlpl` + web-demos registry entry: forward-noise a
   2D dataset (moons) over a linear beta schedule, train a tiny MLP to
   predict the added noise, reverse-sample from noise back onto the data
   manifold, scatter before/after. TDD: an eval test that the trained
   denoiser's reverse samples land closer to the manifold than the
   untrained baseline.

2. **conv2d-primitive** -- `conv2d` (+ `conv_transpose2d` or
   `upsample_nearest`) forward + autograd backward on CPU and the
   device backends; `group_norm`, `silu`, `sin`/`cos` if missing.
   Glossary: Convolution / Conv2d, Group normalization, SiLU. Gradcheck
   parity (CPU) + device parity.

3. **tiny-unet-diffusion** -- a small conv U-Net image diffusion
   (MNIST-scale), trained + sampled under `device("cuda")` /
   `device("mlx")`. Timestep embedding, group_norm, silu, upsample.
   Connect-only demo + literate page.

4. **stable-diffusion-connect** -- real text-to-image: add
   `candle-transformers` to the CUDA/MLX serve build (feature-gated),
   a safetensors pretrained-weight loader, cross-attention + CLIP

# MLPL Multi-Saga Plan

This plan sequences the remaining work from `docs/research2.txt`
(the small-LLM / training-platform vision) against the current
state of the repo. Completed sagas are listed in `docs/saga.md`;
through v0.4 we have the language core, REPL, SVG viz, ML
built-ins, and six end-to-end demos, but every demo still carries
its own hand-written gradients. Everything downstream of autograd
depends on removing that limitation.
